exams.syllabus: ABRSM Woodwind Practical Grades from 2026 (the 2022 lists may still be used until 31 December 2026). Lists read from the board's official syllabus PDF.
comps: 150 total: three pieces 30 each (90), scales and arpeggios 21, sight-reading 21, aural tests 18. Distinction 130-150, Merit 120-129, Pass 100-119 (a pass in every component is not required). UK UCAS points for G6-8 (Pass/Merit/Distinction): G6 8/10/12, G7 12/14/16, G8 18/24/30.

Three pieces, one from each of List A (faster, agile), List B (lyrical, expressive) and List C (varied styles/traditions); the repertoire lists are the same as for Performance Grades. Live piano accompaniment required unless the piece is a solo/study; recorded accompaniment not allowed. At G1-3 some or all pieces may use woodwind accompaniment: DUET pieces (play upper part), DUET/PIANO either. Up to two unaccompanied SOLO pieces may be played. Some grades (e.g. Descant G2, G4; Flute G2, G3, G4, G6, G8; Oboe G1, G4, G6, G8; Clarinet G7; Bassoon G3; Sax G1, G2, G4) require at least one accompanied piece. Listed arrangement/transcription editions must be used; otherwise any edition. Repeats generally not played except short ones; da capo/dal segno followed; cadenzas omitted. May play from memory (examiner needs a copy). Related-instrument options: Descant may play one piece on tenor or treble recorder (then A/B/C lists still apply); Treble G1-5 may play one piece on descant, G6-8 on another recorder where indicated; Saxophones may play one piece (any list) on another saxophone; Flute G8 one piece on alto flute and Oboe G8 one on cor anglais where indicated. Pieces from the 2022 syllabus allowed until 31 Dec 2026 (all requirements from the same syllabus).

Practical Grades are face-to-face exams; ABRSM also offers Performance Grades (separate qualifications focusing on a whole performance) using the same repertoire lists, and digital exams; marks cannot be transferred between Practical and Performance Grades, and using different pieces for both is recommended. Alternative tests exist for specific needs (blind/partially sighted: Braille memory or aural repetition for sight-reading; deaf/hearing-impaired: alternative aural tests).
sections: Scales & technical work
Scales: F, G maj; D min (nat/harm/mel) - 1 oct | Arpeggios: F, G maj; D min - 1 oct | Articulation: tongued/slurred (examiner's choice)
Sight-reading
4 bars; 4/4, 3/4; dotted minims to paired quavers and rests; tongued notes or simple two-note slurs; dynamics (recorders mf only; others f and mf); keys (majors; minors): G, F
Aural & other tests
Clap pulse and say 2 or 3 time; sing back 3 two-bar echoes (major, tonic-mediant); spot a pitch change (near start/end); answer questions on dynamics and articulation of a piece

comps: Face-to-face: 3 pieces x 22 (fluency & accuracy 7, technical facility 7, communication & interpretation 8) = 66; technical work 14; supporting tests 20 (Initial-G5: any two of sight reading, aural, improvisation, musical knowledge, 10 each; G6-8: sight reading 10 + aural or improvisation 10); total 100. Pass 60-74, Merit 75-86, Distinction 87-100 (Below Pass 1: 45-59; Below Pass 2: 0-44). Per piece: Distinction 19-22, Merit 16-18, Pass 13-15. No need to pass every section. Digital technical-work pathway: 3 pieces x 22 = 66, technical work 14, overall performance 20 (=100); digital Repertoire-only pathway: 4 pieces x 25 = 100; same attainment bands. UCAS points G6 8/10/12, G7 12/14/16, G8 18/24/30 (Pass/Merit/Distinction).

Three pieces from the current repertoire list: two accompanied from Group A and one unaccompanied from Group B. At Initial-G3 one Group A piece may be a duet (upper part; duet part on a woodwind instrument, live or recorded). Own composition may replace a piece (accompanied -> Group A, unaccompanied -> Group B), comparable in demand (Initial 0.5-1 min up to G8 3.5-5 min; stave notation required G6-8; no marks for quality of composition). Flute, clarinet and saxophone candidates may swap one piece for a Jazz Woodwind piece listed for the same instrument, grade and group. Instrument rules: piccolo/alto flute, Eb/bass clarinet, cor anglais, contrabassoon only where listed (max one such piece); recorder G6-8 must play both descant and treble, only one piece on tenor/sopranino/bass; no plastic saxophones. Repeats over 4 bars not played; da capo/dal segno observed; no metronomes; memory optional (no extra marks). Accompanist supplied by candidate; backing tracks allowed to G3 face-to-face (live from G4), and at all grades digitally.

Digital exams (filmed, one continuous take, up to 3GB) offer two pathways: Technical work (3 pieces + scales/arpeggios Set A or B, or exercises, or G6-8 orchestral extracts/study, + overall performance mark) or Repertoire-only (4 pieces: at least two Group A and one Group B, 25 marks each). Digital technical work uses the same material as face-to-face (Set A/B subsets); there are no supporting tests digitally.
sections: Scales & technical work

Scales & arpeggios (from memory; examiner selects): scales F, G major, E minor (harmonic/melodic/natural), one octave; arpeggios F, G major, E minor; tongued or slurred, mf; min tempi: scales crotchet=72, arpeggios quaver=120. Either Bb or Eb saxophone. Digital: same material split into fixed Set A or Set B (all from memory); choose one. Or exercises (music may be used): prepare three, one from each pair, and play two (candidate chooses first, examiner the second; digital: choose two from different groups). Tone & phrasing: A Mouthful / Snake in a Basket; articulation: Waltz by Step / The Earthworm; finger technique: Smooth / ...and back again. Technical work and supporting tests may be on Bb or Eb saxophone.
Sight-reading
Unseen extract ~2 grades lower, 30 s preparation; range an octave; keys (cumulative): F, G major.
Aural & other tests

Two of four tests (10 marks each): sight reading; aural; improvisation; musical knowledge. Aural (4-bar melody, major key, 2 or 3 time): clap pulse (3rd hearing); identify dynamic f/p and legato/staccato; last note higher or lower than first (first two bars); spot where a rhythm/pitch change occurs. Improvisation: stylistic - 4 bars played twice (8 bars), F/G major, I/V, fanfare or moderato; motivic - 2-bar fragment, response 4-8 bars, F/G major, up to a major 3rd; harmonic - 4-bar sequence x2, I/V, C major. Musical knowledge: note values, explain key/time signatures, ledger-line notes (up to 2), terms and signs (plus Initial).

General notes

y00721.d: Creston's Concerto for Alto Saxophone: three movements. Practises range and agility.

z00168.d: Romance from Schumann's Three Romances Op. 94, arranged for saxophone; a tender lyrical movement practising sustained tone, breath control and Romantic phrasing.
z00168.rw: Beautiful Schumann, well suited to tenor sax

z00169.d: Allegro from Bach's G minor sonata BWV 1020, transcribed by Harle; a quick, energetic movement practising tonguing, agile fingers and clean articulation.

z00170.d: Molto allegro from Saint-Saëns's sonata, transcribed for alto saxophone; a brisk, brilliant French movement with rapid runs practising agility and tonguing.

z00171.d: Adagio and Allegro from Bach's G minor sonata BWV 1020, transcribed by Harle; a lyrical slow movement and a brisk fast one practising breath, tonguing and phrasing.

z00172.d: Jahrmarkt Scene (fairground scene) from Reinecke's Fantasiestücke, arranged for saxophone; a lively, colourful Romantic movement practising agile fingers and tonguing.

z00173.d: Allegro scherzando from Saint-Saëns's sonata, arranged for saxophone; a light, quick movement with playful rhythms practising agility and articulation.

z00282.d: Tchaikovsky's Hurdy-Gurdy Man from Album for the Young: a drone-like, folksy, simple tune. Practises steady rhythm, tone and short phrases.

z00283.d: Mendelssohn's Song Without Words, Op. 109, originally for cello: a lyrical, flowing Romantic melody. Practises phrasing, tone and expressive rubato.

z00284.d: Fast Allegro vivace from Singelée's first saxophone quartet, here with a bright, virtuosic texture. Practises fast tonguing, agile fingerwork and ensemble.

z00285.d: Albéniz's Tango, a languid Spanish dance with habanera rhythm, arranged for saxophone. Practises rhythmic character, smooth tone and expression.

z00286.d: Choice of Elgar's Chanson de matin (bright morning mood) or Chanson de nuit (darker, night mood). Practises lyrical phrasing and rubato.
z00286.rw: Beloved, tuneful and lovely for sax

z00287.d: Handel's sonata for flute arranged by Marcel Mule: Allegro, Largo and Finale. Practises Baroque style, ornament and varied articulation.

z00288.d: Pastorale and Bourrée by German: a graceful pastoral then a lively dance, Edwardian English style. Practises lyricism and crisp dance rhythm.

z00289.d: Vivaldi's A minor violin concerto arranged for saxophone: bright, flowing Allegro or driving Presto. Practises articulation, speed and Baroque style.

z00290.d: Adagio and Allegro from the Bach sonata in G minor (originally for gamba or flute), arranged by Harle. Practises Baroque style, lyrical line and agility.
